claims.text: The starting material is a multi-element, nearly equiatomic high-entropy alloy catalyst used for automotive exhaust applications.
An ultrathin CeO2 overlayer can be deposited on the catalyst by ALD.
The proposed CeO2 overlayer thickness is approximately 1–3 nm.
ALD will produce a conformal CeO2 film covering and interacting with the catalyst's active surface sites.
The CeO2 overlayer will function as an oxygen buffer through redox-active oxygen-storage capacity.
The CeO2 overlayer will stabilize active sites under cyclic and humid exhaust conditions.
The CeO2 overlayer will reduce surface diffusion of metal atoms.
Reduced metal-atom surface diffusion will inhibit catalyst-particle agglomeration and sintering.
Inhibiting sintering and agglomeration will preserve catalytic activity and extend durability.
Relative to the untreated catalyst, the CeO2-coated catalyst will retain greater catalytic activity after thermal and chemical stress.
The CeO2-coated catalyst will maintain performance under transient, low-temperature conditions containing H2O and NO.
Applying the CeO2 overlayer requires no additional platinum-group metal.
The untreated catalyst undergoes activity loss, sintering, and loss of active sites during transient, humid, low-temperature operation and thermal aging.
The proposed intervention is anticipated to remain effective during thermal aging up to approximately 800°C.
Effectiveness at substantially higher temperatures or under markedly different pollutant loads has not been established.
The optimal CeO2 thickness, coating uniformity, and long-term stability in real exhaust remain undetermined.
